title: Auditor mains take argv[1:]-style; passing prog exited all seven
body: First in-process fan-out passed [rel] as argv[0]; every argparse-based auditor exited 2 on its own filename. The leg recorded all-subprocess fallback with AttributeError-looking noise while ctypes showed the real shape. Fix: argv without prog element. Proof command: tools/deep_dive.py --forensics leg line, all 8 markers read in-process(main). Lesson: when every leg fails identically, the harness is passing the wrong thing, not the legs being broken.

title: msys /tmp is not Windows Python /tmp on this host
body: Seed file written via msys cp to /tmp was unreadable by the 316t interpreter: Git Bash /tmp resolves to the MSYS temp dir while Windows Python /tmp means \tmp on the current drive. Fix: resolve the temp dir from tempfile.gettempdir() in the same interpreter that reads it, then copy there. Proof: seed detected at line 2, strict exit 1, seed deleted. Never assume one /tmp across runtimes.

title: Leading blank line in wsl chunk silently zeroed the denominator
body: First _audit_wsl split on ==FILE== and took lines[0] as the path; a leading newline made every path miss and both distros reported 0 files all-match -- HED-9's exact lie. Fix skips only leading blanks for the path while keeping body bytes intact for hashing. Proof: rerun reads 1 file / 9 blocks per distro, all match. A count of files must count distinct files, fixed the same day with a seen-set.

title: json.dump with sort_keys rewrote all of defaults.json for a 1-line knob
body: Adding the drift_audit knob via json.dump(sort_keys=True) reformatted 173 lines for a single key. Reverted with git checkout and applied a surgical one-line text edit instead: 1 insertion, 0 deletions. Rule: settings files are edited as text; serializers are for reports.

title: Commit blocked on unqualified absence claim, fixed by scoping it
body: Commit message said CLI paths are untouched and the claim guard rejected it under RULE 0B-E as an unqualified absence claim. Fix: scoped the claim to the evidence -- git diff -U0 on the 7 files shows 242 insertions and 0 removed lines, so the CLI code paths in these files are unchanged. Precision, not bypass: no ALLOW_CLAIM_GUARD used.

title: Read outputs double backslashes; ground truth is a character count
body: Two read tools showed regexes with doubled backslashes, suggesting every auditor pattern matched literal backslash sequences. A repair that had demonstrably worked (GUID extracted, entry created, dump-verified) contradicted that reading. Ground truth via Python backslash count: single backslashes, patterns correct. Lesson: when a display and a deed disagree, count characters -- numbers, not glyphs.

title: Ratchet state I/O used silent pass until the scanner objected
body: First _ratchet_load/_ratchet_save caught OSError with bare pass; the staged scanner flagged silent_except_pass twice and blocked the commit. Structural fix, not suppression: failures are recorded into _RATCHET_NOTES and surfaced in the leg detail line. The scanner is right that a state file which cannot be read is a fact the leg must print.

title: Latched per-leg strict exposed auditors that reject --strict
body: The slice-5 ratchet passes --strict to latched auditors; leg_ledger and claim_agreement had no such flag, so a latched run would have died in argparse with exit 2 instead of auditing. Fixed at the source with accepted no-op --strict flags (findings already fail; BLIND stays instrument-state). Lesson: any flag a harness can pass must be accepted by every leg it fans out to.

title: Latched strict turned three advisory debts into leg failures
body: Once 7 auditors latched strict, settings_shadow, head_audit and truncation failed on pre-existing findings: the orphan mcp_stack.floor_auth_mode knob, foreign-lane ELIZA dirt (hands off), and silent truncation sites. Forensics exit went 0 to 1 with the debts named. This is the ratchet working as designed, not a regression from the slices; each debt predates the work and shows in the first baseline run.
